Then implement and validate in this same conversation and workspace. Fix any independently reported failures before delivery. The complete engineering contract is:

Implement dpath.exact.get_exact(root,segments,default=marker). Paths are finite component iterables, never plain strings; mapping keys retain actual hashable types and punctuation, list indices are nonnegative int excluding bool. Empty path returns root identity. Missing key/index returns an explicit default or raises original error, while invalid traversal/type errors propagate. Do not interpret glob characters, coerce "1" to integer, trigger defaultdict creation, or mutate input; preserve old dpath.get.

Deliver meaningful original-failing public regression tests at library/development_tests/test_development_dp_exact_dev.py and concise English compatibility documentation at library/docs/development-dp-exact-dev.md. Preserve all frozen original tests, dependency metadata and test controls. Change only authorized paths.

Root depth zero and node budget includes root/containers. Empty containers are leaves; optional nonempty containers are emitted too. Implement dpath.patches.apply_edits(root,operations) using completed get_exact for typed literal paths. Materialize operations first and work on a deep copy. Support add/replace/remove/test; dictionary add sets a key, replace/remove require it, list add inserts at 0..len and remove compacts. Reject bool/negative list indices; test compares recursive types and values so True differs from 1. Empty path may test or replace/add root, but cannot remove root. Any later invalid operation, failed test or enumeration error leaves original unchanged; copy incoming mutable values and do not reinterpret paths as globs.

Materialize and validate both record iterables before merging: every mapping has a hashable business key and no duplicates within a side, using (type,value) identity so bool/int/string keys are not silently conflated.
